tools.name: airnxt_batch_import_logbook_entries
tools.description:
Bulk import logbook entries from a JSON file. Uses PUT /logbook-entry (upsert) — re-importing same data updates existing records, not duplicates.

Import rules enforced automatically on every entry:
- **Status forced to "close"** — imported entries are always finalized
- **Planned = Actual**: plannedTripAirports copied to actualTripAirports if actual is missing; same for timings
- **Hours → Minutes conversion**: Flight time fields (flightMinutesAB, flightMinutesBB) auto-converted from hours to minutes (default). Set flightTimeUnit='minutes' to skip conversion.
- **Auto-sequence flightLogNumber**: If generalInfo.flightLogNumber is missing, auto-generates sequential numbers per asset (e.g. "FLT-0001", "FLT-0002")
- **Chronological sort**: Entries sorted by departure date/time ascending before processing
- **Upsert**: PUT method ensures re-import updates existing records
- **Rate limiting**: Configurable delay between concurrent batches to avoid API overload
- **Retry**: Transient failures (429, 5xx) are retried with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)

Features:
- **UUID pre-validation**: Verifies all referenced asset UUIDs exist before sending any entries
- **Duplicate detection**: Warns about duplicate flightLogNumber values per asset
- **Dry run**: Validate everything without sending to API
- **Resumable**: Use startIndex to resume after a partial failure

The JSON file must contain an array of logbook entry objects:

{
  "generalInfo": { "assetId": "uuid", "flightLogNumber": "FLT-001" },
  "type": "flight",
  "crew": { "pilot": { "id": "uuid", "isFlying": true }, "coPilot": { "id": "uuid", "isFlying": false } },
  "plannedTripAirports": { "departureId": "uuid", "arrivalId": "uuid" },
  "plannedTripTiming": { "blockDepartureDateTime": "ISO", "takeOffDateTime": "ISO", "touchDownDateTime": "ISO", "blockArrivalDateTime": "ISO", "flightMinutesAB": 5.5, "flightMinutesBB": 6.0 },
  "delays": [{ "typeId": "uuid", "time": 30 }],
  "events": [{ "typeId": "uuid", "time": "ISO" }],
  "logId": "uuid (optional, for upsert matching)"
}

Returns a summary with success/failure counts and details of any errors.

filePath.description: Absolute path to JSON file containing array of logbook entry objects

rateLimitMs.description: Delay in milliseconds between each concurrent batch (default: 200). Prevents API overload. Set to 0 to disable.

flightTimeUnit.description: Unit for flightMinutesAB/flightMinutesBB in the source data. Default: 'hours' (auto-converts to minutes). Set 'minutes' if data is already in minutes.

flightLogNumberPrefix.description: Prefix for auto-generated flightLogNumbers when missing from entries. Default: 'FLT'

dryRun.description: If true, validate structure + UUIDs + duplicates + show transformations without sending to API

startIndex.description: Start from this index (0-based) — useful for resuming after a partial failure

maxEntries.description: Max entries to process in this batch (useful for testing with a small subset first)

skipValidation.description: Skip UUID pre-validation and duplicate checks (faster, use if data is already verified)

skipSort.description: Skip chronological sorting (use if file is already in correct order)

tools.name: airnxt_set_requirement_applicability
tools.description: Replace the applicability condition set for a requirement (PUT /engineering-requirements/:id/applicability). This is the ONLY way to change applicability once a requirement is ACTIVE — PATCH /engineering-requirements/:id is blocked on active requirements ("Cannot update an active requirement"). The call REPLACES the entire condition set (not a merge); the requirement stays active and the parent document stays approved. Saving emits requirement.updated, which triggers automatic re-resolution (asset + component applicability recompute) — no manual resolve call needed. Condition types: AIRCRAFT_MODEL, AIRCRAFT_REGISTRATION, AIRCRAFT_SERIAL, PART_NUMBER, PART_NUMBER_SERIAL. Operators: equal | isOneOf (PART_NUMBER_SERIAL always uses equal; its value is {partNumber, serialNumber}). Provide conditions via `rules` (a JSON object in EITHER the legacy rule-engine dialect {"all"|"any": [{"fact": "aircraftModel|serialNumber|registration|partNumber|partSerialNumber", "operator"?, "value"}]} or the wire dialect {"logic": "ALL"|"ANY", "conditions": [{"type", "operator"?, "value"}]}) — auto-normalized — or via `conditions` (a JSON array of wire-form {type, operator?, value} objects) together with `logic`. Backend validation errors (400 — empty conditions, bad operator, cross-scope ANY group) pass through verbatim.

logic.description: Combine conditions with AND (ALL) or OR (ANY). Required when using `conditions` instead of `rules`.

conditions.description: JSON array of wire-form conditions: [{"type": "AIRCRAFT_MODEL", "operator"?: "equal|isOneOf", "value": "..."|["..."]}]. Use together with `logic`. Alternative to `rules`.

rules.description: JSON object of applicability rules in EITHER dialect — legacy rule-engine {"all"|"any": [{"fact", "operator"?, "value"}]} or wire form {"logic", "conditions"} — normalized automatically. Alternative to `conditions` + `logic`.

tools.name: airnxt_batch_recalculate_requirements
tools.description: Recalculate persisted component due values for many requirements (POST /engineering-requirements/:id/recalculate per requirement, run in batches). USE THIS AFTER changing limits outside the app — a raw SQL edit to requirement_limits emits no requirement.updated event, and the daily calendar sweep only looks 90 days ahead, so rows due further out never refresh on their own and the UI keeps serving the old date. Also the tool for applying a formula fix to existing rows or replaying a failed sweep. TARGETING: pass `documentRefNumber` to auto-enumerate every requirement of a document (paged, up to 100/page), or `requirementIds` for an explicit list. Exactly one is required. Non-active requirements are skipped automatically (the endpoint 409s on draft/archived). `calendarOnly: true` restricts to requirements whose thresholds are days/months/years — the only ones whose due DATE depends on thresholds_effective_date; flight-hour and cycle limits never read it in the component engine. Start with `dryRun: true` to see the enumerated set, its status split, and the thresholds_effective_date distribution before enqueuing anything. ASYNC: a 202 means jobs were ENQUEUED, not that any value changed — verify with airnxt_get_requirement_component_statuses and watch nextDueDate advance. Safe to re-run: the endpoint is idempotent for the same inputs.

requirementIds.description: Explicit list of requirement UUIDs to recalculate. Mutually exclusive with documentRefNumber. Status is not pre-checked for this path — non-active IDs surface as 409 failures.

inventoryItemIds.description: Restrict the recalculation to specific components. Applied to EVERY targeted requirement, so this is normally only meaningful with a single requirementId. Omit to recalculate every open component. An empty array is REJECTED rather than treated as 'omitted', which would widen the scope to all components.

reason.description: Free text written to the job log for audit. Strongly recommended.

calendarOnly.description: Only recalculate requirements with a days/months/years threshold — the set whose due date depends on thresholds_effective_date. Requires documentRefNumber (threshold units are unknown for a bare ID list). Default false.

includeInactive.description: Include draft/archived requirements, which the endpoint rejects with 409. Default false. Enable only to prove which ones are inactive.

dryRun.description: Enumerate, classify and report the target set WITHOUT enqueuing anything. Default false.

concurrency.description: Parallel requests per batch. Default 5, clamped to [1,20].

rateLimitMs.description: Delay between batches in ms. Default 200. Set 0 to disable.

startIndex.description: Resume from this index in the target list. Default 0.

tools.name: airnxt_batch_import_parts
tools.description:
Bulk import parts from an Excel (.xlsx/.xls) or JSON file into the AirNxt parts catalog.

Rows are deduplicated by part number — only unique part numbers are created.

2. Validate structure (each row needs Part Number + Part Description minimum)
3. Deduplicate by part number (keeps first occurrence, counts duplicates)
4. Resolve manufacturer (by name or UUID)
5. Dry run gate (validate without sending to API)
6. Batch process with retry (POST /parts per unique part number)

Supports concurrency control, rate limiting, resume from index, and dry-run mode.

tools.name: airnxt_batch_import_requirements
tools.description:
Bulk import maintenance requirements from Excel files into AirNxt.

Supports MRB tasks, TLMC tasks, Engine LLP (life-limited parts), and STC tasks.
Auto-detects sheet type from sheet name. Filters rows by effectivity (only imports tasks applicable to the specified aircraft MSN).

Import pipeline:
1. Read Excel file (auto-detects columns per sheet type)
2. Filter by effectivity — only rows with YES/Y for the aircraft MSN
3. Resolve or auto-create parent engineering document (MPD type)
4. Transform rows: parse task intervals → limits, extract ATA chapters, build requirement payloads
5. Dry run gate (validate without sending to API)
6. Batch POST /engineering-requirements with retry

Interval parsing: "2400 H" → flight_hours, "48 M" → months, "15000 CYC" → cycles, combined "2400 H / 48 M" → whichever_occurs_first
Engine LLP: life limits as one_time type with thresholds

For multi-sheet files (e.g., TLMC with ENGINE LLP and STLMC sheets), run once per sheet using the sheetName parameter.
Use airnxt_batch_import_requirements({ filePath, sheetName: "ENGINE LLP", ... }) for engine LLP data.

Each entry is validated + normalized via the shared validateRequirementRow (strict schema, ATA→4-digit, applicabilityRules→rule-engine, repetitive limits auto-filled); invalid rows are skipped + reported.

tools.name: airnxt_reauth
tools.description: Force re-authentication with AirNxt. Deletes the cached access token at ~/.airnxt-mcp-tokens.json, triggers a fresh Auth0 PKCE browser login (opens system browser; user completes login on login.airnxt.ai — multi-org operators see Auth0's organization picker), then decodes the issued JWT and returns the active org context (Auth0 org_id + AirNxt organizationId UUID + organization name) plus token expiry. Use when tools fail with 401/403, after switching environments or accounts, or when you need to switch the active customer org. Blocks for up to 120 seconds waiting for the user to complete the browser login. Note: org confirmation is JWT-derived — the AirNxt /user/profile endpoint is unreliable for multi-org users due to a known backend bug, so this tool reads the org claim straight from the access token.

tools.name: airnxt_whoami
tools.description: Read-only environment + identity check. Does NOT re-authenticate or open a browser. Reports the ACTIVE environment (STAGE / PROD / UNKNOWN, derived from the resolved token's aud/iss), the org (Auth0 org_id + AirNxt organizationId + name), the API base URL, and token validity/expiry. Reads the token getAccessToken() would use (AIRNXT_ACCESS_TOKEN env override first, then the cached token — never the cache alone), so it reflects what writes will actually hit. Use this BEFORE any write to confirm you are on the intended environment/org. Flags a token/API env mismatch. If AIRNXT_EXPECTED_ENV is set, writes that don't match it are refused server-side.

tools.name: airnxt_list_asset_crs_signoffs
tools.description:
List all Certificate of Release to Service (CRS) sign-offs for a given asset.

A CRS sign-off is a regulatory artifact certifying an aircraft is airworthy after maintenance.
Use this tool to verify sign-off history or audit compliance status for a specific asset.

Use airnxt_get_asset or airnxt_list_assets to obtain the assetId.

assetId.description: UUID of the asset whose CRS sign-offs to list.

tools.name: airnxt_create_crs_signoff
tools.description:
Create a Certificate of Release to Service (CRS) sign-off, certifying an aircraft is airworthy after maintenance.

A CRS is a regulatory artifact attached to a completed logbook entry and signed by a licensed engineer.

**Required fields (4):**
- `assetId` — UUID of the asset being certified. Use airnxt_get_asset to find it.
- `crsSignOffEngineer` — Object describing the signing engineer (must include `name`; optionally `id`, `license`, `certification`). Use airnxt_list_employees to find a candidate engineer.
- `crsSignOffDateTime` — ISO 8601 datetime of the sign-off (e.g. "2026-05-08T14:30:00Z").
- `logbookEntryModelId` — UUID of the logbook entry this CRS is attached to. Use airnxt_create_logbook_entry or airnxt_list_logbook_entries to find it.

**Optional fields:**
- `crsSignOffAmoRef` — AMO reference string (e.g. "AMO-UAE-145-001").
- `crsSignOffStation` — Station where the sign-off occurred.
- `crsStatus` — "valid" (default) or "invalid".
- `setAsCurrent` — Boolean; marks this as the active CRS for the asset (default false).

assetId.description: UUID of the asset this CRS applies to. Obtain via airnxt_get_asset or airnxt_list_assets.

name.description: Full name of the signing engineer

crsSignOffEngineer.description: Engineer who signed off the CRS. Must include at least `name`; may include `id`, `license`, `certification`, and any additional fields.

crsSignOffDateTime.description: ISO 8601 datetime when the CRS was signed (e.g. '2026-05-08T14:30:00Z').

logbookEntryModelId.description: UUID of the logbook entry this CRS is attached to. Obtain via airnxt_create_logbook_entry or airnxt_list_logbook_entries.

crsSignOffStation.description: Station / airport where the sign-off occurred (e.g. 'Dubai International Airport').

setAsCurrent.description: If true, marks this as the active CRS for the asset. Default: false.

tools.name: airnxt_list_work_orders
tools.description: List all work orders in the organisation. Supports optional free-text search, sort direction, and pagination. Results are paginated (default 10 per page) — always check the returned pagination.total_pages and walk `page` to the end before concluding a set is complete. Returns work order UUIDs needed for airnxt_get_work_order, airnxt_list_work_order_tasks, airnxt_update_work_order_planning, and airnxt_start_work_order.

search.description: Free-text search across work order fields (optional)

sortOrder.description: Sort direction for results. Default: DESC

tools.name: airnxt_get_work_order
tools.description: Retrieve a single work order by UUID, including its full detail (status, asset, planned dates, tasks summary, etc.). Use airnxt_list_work_orders to find the id.

id.description: UUID of the work order to retrieve (use airnxt_list_work_orders)

tools.name: airnxt_list_work_order_tasks
tools.description: List all tasks belonging to a work order. Returns task UUIDs needed for airnxt_get_work_order_task and airnxt_toggle_work_order_task. Use airnxt_list_work_orders to find the work order id.

id.description: UUID of the work order whose tasks to list (use airnxt_list_work_orders)

tools.name: airnxt_get_work_order_task
tools.description: Retrieve the full detail of a single task within a work order, including completion status, assigned personnel, materials, and limits. Use airnxt_list_work_order_tasks to find the taskId.

woId.description: UUID of the parent work order (use airnxt_list_work_orders)

taskId.description: UUID of the task to retrieve (use airnxt_list_work_order_tasks)

tools.name: airnxt_update_work_order_planning
tools.description: Update the planning details of a work order: planned start date and/or estimated downtime (in hours). Both fields are optional — supply only the fields you want to change. Use airnxt_list_work_orders to find the work order id.

plannedStartDate.description: ISO 8601 datetime for the planned start of work (e.g. '2026-06-01T08:00:00Z'). Must be a valid ISO 8601 datetime string; offsets/timezone suffixes are accepted.

estimatedDowntime.description: Estimated downtime in hours (e.g. 4.5 for 4 hours 30 min)

tools.name: airnxt_start_work_order

id.description: UUID of the work order to start (use airnxt_list_work_orders)

description.description: Optional note or description recorded when starting the work order

tools.name: airnxt_toggle_work_order_task

woId.description: UUID of the parent work order (use airnxt_list_work_orders)

taskId.description: UUID of the task to toggle (use airnxt_list_work_order_tasks)

tools.name: airnxt_get_position
tools.description: Get details for a component position (e.g. ENG-1, APU) by its UUID — code, name, and configuration context.

tools.name: airnxt_get_position_compliance
tools.description: Get P/N-based compliance status for all components on a position — which engineering requirements apply and their status for the components currently installed there.

tools.name: airnxt_get_position_ri_history

tools.name: airnxt_list_mct
tools.description: List Master Configuration Templates with filtering (status, aircraft type, IPC doc ref, created/updated by, date ranges) and pagination. Returns template UUIDs needed by the other MCT tools.

aircraftTypeId.description: Filter by one or more aircraft type UUIDs (from airnxt_lookup_aircraft_types)

createdFrom.description: ISO date lower bound for createdOn

createdTo.description: ISO date upper bound for createdOn

tools.name: airnxt_get_mct
tools.description: Get a Master Configuration Template header by UUID (aircraft type, IPC ref, revision, draft/published status, publish metadata). Use airnxt_get_mct_tree for the node tree.

tools.name: airnxt_get_mct_tree
tools.description: Get an MCT's node tree. By default returns a summary (counts by level) plus only operator-added (non-system) nodes — the raw tree includes ~475 system-managed ATA-skeleton nodes. Filter by ataChapterCode (with includeSystemNodes=true) to find a Level-2 anchor UUID to attach to. Set full=true to return the entire flat node list.

ataChapterCode.description: Filter returned nodes by ATA chapter code (e.g. '32'); pair with includeSystemNodes=true to locate a skeleton anchor

includeSystemNodes.description: Include system-managed skeleton nodes in the returned list (default false). Counts always cover all nodes.

full.description: Return the entire flat node list verbatim (can be large). Default false.

tools.name: airnxt_create_mct
tools.description: Create a Master Configuration Template for an aircraft type. The server auto-seeds a system-managed ATA-chapter skeleton (~475 assembly nodes); you then attach assemblies/positions under a Level-2 node. Returns the new template (DRAFT).

tools.name: airnxt_create_mct_node
tools.description: Add one node (assembly or position) to a DRAFT MCT under an existing parent (parentNodeId must be level >= 2). For building a whole subtree in one call, prefer airnxt_create_mct_tree.

parentNodeId.description: Parent assembly node UUID (must already exist, level >= 2)

itemPositionId.description: Required for POSITION nodes; unique within parent

tools.name: airnxt_batch_upsert_mct_nodes
tools.description: Low-level batch create/update of MCT nodes (one level at a time). Every create's parentNodeId MUST already exist — intra-batch parent refs are NOT supported (the whole batch rolls back with PARENT_NODE_NOT_FOUND). For nested subtrees, use airnxt_create_mct_tree, which chains levels for you. For large batches, pass nodesFilePath (an absolute path to a JSON file {creates?:[...], updates?:[...]}) instead of the inline arrays so the payload never passes through the agent.

creates.description: Nodes to create (inline). All parents must already exist. Mutually exclusive with nodesFilePath.

nodeId.description: UUID of the existing node to update

updates.description: Existing nodes to update (inline). Mutually exclusive with nodesFilePath.

nodesFilePath.description: Absolute path to a JSON file shaped { creates?: [...], updates?: [...] } (same shapes as the inline arrays). The server reads + validates it directly. Mutually exclusive with creates/updates.

tools.name: airnxt_create_mct_tree
tools.description: Create a nested subtree of assemblies/positions under an existing anchor in a DRAFT MCT, in one call. Builds level-by-level (one batch per depth), chaining real UUIDs down — the only reliable way to create parent+child together. POSITION nodes must be leaves.

parentNodeId.description: Existing anchor node UUID to attach the subtree under (level >= 2; find one via airnxt_get_mct_tree)

ataChapterCode.description: Required for ASSEMBLY nodes (free-text ATA code, e.g. '32' or '32-10')

itemPositionId.description: Required for POSITION nodes; unique within the parent (e.g. '001')

children.description: Child nodes; POSITION nodes must be leaves (no children)

nodes.description: Nested tree of nodes to create under the anchor

tools.name: airnxt_update_mct_node
tools.description: Update a single MCT node (rename, re-parent, change ATA/position fields, sort order). Re-parenting triggers a cycle check on the server.

parentNodeId.description: New parent assembly UUID within the same template

itemPositionId.description: POSITION nodes only; uniqueness re-checked against new parent

tools.name: airnxt_list_node_applicable_parts
tools.description: List the set of part numbers approved for installation at a position node.

tools.name: airnxt_add_node_applicable_part
tools.description: Associate a catalog part (P/N) with a position node — declares that part as installable at this position. The part must be an existing, active catalog part (from airnxt_list_parts).

partId.description: Catalog part UUID (parts.id) to allow at this position

tools.name: airnxt_remove_node_applicable_part
tools.description: Remove a part (P/N) from a position node's set of approved parts.

partId.description: Catalog part UUID to remove from this position

tools.name: airnxt_batch_add_node_applicable_parts
tools.description: Associate many catalog parts (P/Ns) with position nodes in one call — a batch wrapper over airnxt_add_node_applicable_part. Each item is an independent { nodeId, partId } pair (repeat a nodeId to add several parts to one position); failures are aggregated per-item, not short-circuited. Identical pairs are de-duplicated before any POST. Assembly nodes or published (immutable) templates fail per-item with the API's reason — there is no preflight. Use dryRun to preview; lower concurrency if you see 503s. For large batches, pass itemsFilePath (absolute path to a JSON array of {nodeId, partId}) instead of items.

partId.description: Catalog part UUID (parts.id) to allow at this position

items.description: Pairs to associate (inline). Identical (nodeId, partId) pairs are de-duplicated. Mutually exclusive with itemsFilePath.

itemsFilePath.description: Absolute path to a JSON file containing the array of {nodeId, partId} pairs (same shape as items[]). The server reads + validates it directly. Mutually exclusive with items.

dryRun.description: Preview (with dedupe) without making any POST calls

concurrency.description: Max parallel POSTs. Default 3 (stays under staging's burst-503 threshold)

rateLimitMs.description: Delay in ms between batches. Default 200

startIndex.description: Resume from this index in the de-duplicated list (0-based)

maxEntries.description: Optional cap on items processed (after startIndex)

tools.name: airnxt_publish_mct
tools.description: Publish a DRAFT MCT, making it immutable and available as an induction source. Preflight verifies the template is draft and has at least one position node.

tools.name: airnxt_delete_mct_node
tools.description: Delete an MCT node (and its subtree) from a DRAFT template. Destructive. Fails on system-managed skeleton nodes and on published (immutable) templates.

tools.name: airnxt_list_induction_eligible
tools.description: List aircraft eligible for induction (aircraft-category assets not yet inducted). Returns assetId + aircraftTypeId needed by airnxt_induct_aircraft. Optionally filter to those compatible with a specific published template.

templateId.description: Filter to aircraft eligible for this published MCT (matching aircraft type)

tools.name: airnxt_list_induction_directory
tools.description: List inducted aircraft (the asset-tree directory), paginated. Returns induction records with lifecycleState and node counts. Use airnxt_get_induction / airnxt_get_induction_workspace for detail.

tools.name: airnxt_prepare_induction
tools.description: Resolve a registration + (optional) aircraft-type/template into a ready-to-use airnxt_induct_aircraft payload. Confirms the aircraft is induction-eligible, finds the matching PUBLISHED template, and validates the template's aircraft type matches the asset's. Returns candidates to choose from when more than one published template fits.

templateId.description: Specific published MCT to use; omit to auto-resolve the one published template for the type

tools.name: airnxt_induct_aircraft
tools.description: Induct an aircraft: compose an asset with a PUBLISHED Master Configuration Template, copying its position tree onto the asset. The asset must be aircraft-category and not already inducted; the template must be published and match the asset's aircraft type. Prefer airnxt_prepare_induction to resolve the ids first.

assetId.description: Aircraft asset UUID (must be aircraft-category and not yet inducted)

sourceTemplateId.description: PUBLISHED MCT UUID to source the position tree from

tools.name: airnxt_get_induction
tools.description: Get an induction record header by asset/induction UUID (aircraft, source template, lifecycleState, KPIs). Use airnxt_get_induction_workspace for the position tree.

tools.name: airnxt_get_induction_workspace
tools.description: Get an induction's position tree. By default returns the aircraft header, KPIs, counts by state, and only the POSITION nodes that still need resolving (state UNKNOWN or MISSING) — the raw tree inherits the ~475-node ATA skeleton. Pass state to filter to one state (UNKNOWN|INSTALLED|EMPTY|MISSING), or full=true for the entire node list.

state.description: Show only positions in this state (default: actionable = UNKNOWN + MISSING)

includeSystemNodes.description: Include system-managed skeleton nodes in the returned positions (default false)

full.description: Return the entire flat node list verbatim (can be large). Default false.

tools.name: airnxt_get_induction_metrics
tools.description: Get lightweight KPI metrics for an induction (lifecycleState + counts: total / unknown / installed / empty / missing) without the full position tree.

tools.name: airnxt_resolve_induction_position
tools.description: Resolve one induction position. action=MARK_EMPTY records the position as having no component (omit all component fields). action=INSTALL records an as-installed component and REQUIRES serialNumber + certificate (filePath from airnxt_upload_logistics_certificate_file) + all three life counters (sinceNew, sinceLastInspection, sinceOverhaul). Find unresolved positionIds via airnxt_get_induction_workspace.

action.description: INSTALL a component, or MARK_EMPTY (no component)

serialNumber.description: Installed component serial number (required for INSTALL)

filePath.description: GCS file path of the release certificate (from airnxt_upload_logistics_certificate_file)

tools.name: airnxt_batch_resolve_induction_positions
tools.description: Resolve many positions on ONE induction in a single call — a batch wrapper over airnxt_resolve_induction_position. Each entry is INSTALL (serialNumber of an EXISTING inventory item + certificate.filePath + the three life counters) or MARK_EMPTY. Items are independent: a malformed INSTALL entry fails per-item with no API call and the rest proceed. Defaults to concurrency=1 because every entry mutates the SAME induction aggregate and the API does not retry 409/422 state conflicts — raise it only once staging proves same-induction parallelism is safe. Use dryRun to validate payloads (surfaces INSTALL missing-field errors) before any write.

action.description: INSTALL a component, or MARK_EMPTY (no component at this position)

serialNumber.description: INSTALL: serial number of an EXISTING inventory item

filePath.description: GCS file path of the release certificate (from airnxt_upload_logistics_certificate_file)

positions.description: Positions to resolve on this induction (inline). Mutually exclusive with positionsFilePath.

positionsFilePath.description: Absolute path to a JSON file containing the array of position-resolve entries (same shape as positions[]). The server reads + validates it directly. Mutually exclusive with positions.

dryRun.description: Validate payloads (incl. INSTALL required fields) without making any POST calls

concurrency.description: Max parallel resolves. Default 1 — same induction aggregate; 409/422 conflicts are not retried

rateLimitMs.description: Delay in ms between batches. Default 50 (the serial path needs little pacing)

startIndex.description: Resume from this index in positions (0-based)

maxEntries.description: Optional cap on positions processed (after startIndex)

tools.name: airnxt_close_induction
tools.description: Close an induction session (finalizes the as-installed configuration). Preflight verifies the induction is not already completed and blocks if any positions are unresolved (UNKNOWN) or required-but-empty (MISSING) — the API refuses to close otherwise.
